Oral Order
9 19-06-2023
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned A.P.P. for the State and learned counsel for the informant.
The petitioners apprehend their arrest in a case registered for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420 and 504/34 of the Indian Penal Code.
Learned counsel for the informant submits that petitioners earlier had entered into an agreement for sale for a piece of land.
It is further submitted that in consideration of the agreement amount was paid but the said agreement was cancelled later and the entire amount was returned.

It is next submitted that thereafter the petitioners again approached the Patna High Court CR. MISC.
No.5815 of 2020(9) dt.19-06-2023 informant for selling the same piece of land and the informant believing the bona fides of the petitioners again entered into an agreement with respect to the same piece of land but this time for a consideration amount of Rs.10,60,000/-.
It is also submitted that thereafter Rs.9,00,000/- and odd amount was paid but the petitioners have refused to register the land.

Learned counsel further submits that earlier when the agreement was entered and the same was cancelled after the amount was returned as such the informant was sanguine that this time the Shyam Choudhary vs The State Of Bihar on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117038579/
1 petitioners will definitely sell his land and in the event if the land is not sold then the amount would be returned.

entities.text: Shyam Choudhary vs The State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is next submitted that this time the informant was deceived as neither the registry was done nor the payment was returned.

Learned counsel for the petitioners rebuts the submissions of the learned counsel for the informant and submits that no agreement as alleged was entered after the first agreement was cancelled and the money was returned.

It is further submitted that if any payment was made by the informant to the petitioners in pursuance of the present agreement then the same must have been paid by cheque or by cash but then there is no averment in the counter affidavit that how the amount was paid.
Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.5815 of 2020(9) dt.19-06-2023 Learned counsel for the informant at this stage submits that he has instruction that some amount was paid by way of cheque which was credited in the account of the petitioners after the present agreement was entered into but submits that he will seek instruction in the matter.
Put up this case on 26.06.2023.

(Satyavrat Verma, J) Kundan/-
